title: Define structured eligibility outcomes including capacity truncation

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## The PHP analyzer landing on `develop` moves the eligibility numbers by half

PR #6 (`feature/php-analyzer`, merged as `3945aa3`) added `php` to `FileLanguage` and `.php` / `.phtml` to `getFileLanguage`. Recomputed against all 1,792 annotations:

| | annotations ingest cannot open |
| --- | ---: |
| before the PHP analyzer | 960 (54%) |
| **after** | **517 (29%)** |
| moved into scope | **443** |

Per packet:

| packet | ineligible before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| wordpress | 243 / 243 | **0 / 243** |
| drupal | 65 / 65 | **0 / 65** |
| magento | 217 / 217 | **82 / 217** (the remainder is `.xml`) |

Still ineligible by extension: `.rb` 415, `.xml` 82, `.swift` 18, `.example` 2. So the "seven effectively unreadable packets" figure quoted across this epic is now **four** — discourse, spree and redmine on Ruby, plus vapor on Swift.

## What this changes

**Correct the numbers wherever they are quoted as current.** 960/1,792 and "7 packets" appear in several issue descriptions and in the earlier review comments. Those were true when measured and are now stale. The earlier comments stand as a record of the pre-PHP state; the issue descriptions should be corrected, since people plan from them.

**A new requirement for the baseline fingerprint.** This is the important part. Ingest language support is now a variable that moves headline recall by a large margin without any detector change — 443 annotations became eligible from a language analyzer alone. Two baselines taken across a language-support change are not comparable, and nothing in the fingerprint block currently records it.

Recommend the baseline artifact record **the ingest language set** (the `FileLanguage` union, or a digest of it) alongside the scanner commit, and that a change to it start a new series with a bridge run, exactly as a contract change does. Without that, the first time someone adds Ruby the numbers jump and the artifact gives no way to tell that from a detector improvement.

**Worth noting explicitly, because it looks like the thing this epic forbids and is not.** The PHP analyzer was independent language work, not a move to improve a score. But its effect on the corpus is precisely the "fake eval win" pattern the epic warns about, arriving by an honest route. That is the argument for the fingerprint requirement rather than an argument against the analyzer.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Recommendation after PHP landed

Approve the structured outcome model, but describe the PHP result as a static capability change rather than completed eligibility evidence.

The 443 PHP annotations are no longer statically unsupported by extension. They are now potentially processable. They have not yet been proven successfully processed for every relevant layer, which is the condition this contract requires before they enter a denominator. The supported corpus materialization command is also currently broken, so extension counting must not be presented as a completed per-layer run.

Actual eligibility must come only from the structured ledger. The effective capability profile should be layer-specific and include language and extension handling, registered analyzer support, exclusion policy, sensitive-path policy, and file-size, file-count, and byte caps. A global FileLanguage union is insufficient because ingest recognition and layer processing are different capabilities.

Keep the measured 517 annotations as statically unsupported by current extension handling, and label the 443 as newly capability-reachable pending ledger evidence. No baseline should turn either static count directly into successfully processed scope.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Ratified

**The structured outcome model is approved, and the PHP result is a static capability change rather than completed eligibility evidence.**

- The 443 PHP annotations are no longer statically unsupported by extension. They are **capability-reachable pending ledger evidence** — not proven successfully processed per layer, which is the condition this contract requires before anything enters a denominator.
- The 517 remaining stay classified as statically unsupported by current extension handling.
- Actual eligibility comes only from the structured per-layer ledger. Extension counting is never presented as a completed run — the corpus materialization command is currently broken, so no per-layer run has happened.
- The effective capability profile is **per layer** and covers language and extension handling, registered analyzer support, exclusion policy, sensitive-path policy, and file-size, file-count and byte caps. A global `FileLanguage` union is insufficient, because ingest recognition and layer processing are different capabilities.
- No baseline turns either static count directly into successfully processed scope.

This supersedes the framing in my earlier comment, which described the 443 as having moved into scope. They became potentially processable; that is not the same claim.

Closing.
